newsitem.title: USA: GM asked to pay up to $75 million in crash lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: GM asked to pay up to $75 million in crash lawsuit.

text.p: An attorney for a woman who suffered severe brain damage in the crash of a Chevrolet van asked a jury Wednesday to order General Motors Corp. to pay $50 million to $75 million in punitive damages.

In opening arguments in the punitive damages phase of a product liability trial, Chris Searcy, representing plaintiff Therese Hunter, described such an award as "extremely conservative and reasonable under the circumstances."

The same jury on Dec. 20 awarded $25.4 million to the family of Hunter, 45, a former Jacksonville resident who now lives in a Miami assisted living centre. That compensatory damage award exceeded the $15 million to $21.5 million requested by Hunter's attorneys for her medical care.
On March 3, 1991, the 1990 Astro van Hunter was driving was hit by a truck and pushed into a concrete light pole. The impact dislodged the van's steering column and rammed it into her jaw and skull.
The jury found that General Motors, which made Hunter's van, was responsible for her crippling injuries.
Searcy told the jury that an award of $50 million to $75 million would "cause corporate America to cut out the cancer that allows profit to be put ahead of human safety."
In his opening statement, GM attorney Thom Rumberger called the initial jury award of $25 million "shocking and dismaying.
He said he would introduce evidence to show GM was a "responsible ... concerned and loving company."
Circuit Judge Lawrence Fay has said the punitive damages phase of the trial will last no more than three days.
